newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Finland not seeking NATO membership, PM says.
newsitem.headline: Finland not seeking NATO membership, PM says.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen reiterated on Wednesday that his country, which shares a long border with Russia, was not seeking to become a member of the 16-nation North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
"As to Finnish membership in NATO, it is not in the cards," Lipponen told a press conference in Brussels after meeting NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.

Lipponen, who also met Secretary-General Jose Cutileiro of the Western European Union, the European Union's nascent defence arm, said Finland was no longer a neutral country as it was during the Cold War.
Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, Finland describes itself as militarily non-aligned with an independent defence, a policy Lipponen said best serves Finnish interests.

Finland takes part in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme designed to bring together forces across the former Cold War divide and Lipponen said he was looking forward to seeing the planned enhanced version of that cooperation take form.
"We are interested in taking part in the planning activities for future operations," he said.
Lipponen also said Finland was ready to participate in the follow-up force for Bosnia with some 300 troops.

In talks with Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Lipponen stressed that all central and eastern European countries applying for EU membership should be treated equally, referring especially to the three Baltic states.
"Estonia should have as good an opportunity to become a member as any other applicant country," he said.
